title: Airgap bundle composition + Terraform module draft
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working draft describing how we want to compose air-gapped install bundles for Private deployments, and the complementary Terraform module interface that teams will use to install and upgrade those bundles in on-prem / isolated VPC environments. Goal: reduce ad-hoc scripts, make upgrades reproducible, and enable ops teams to validate and pre-seed registries in a repeatable way.

High-level approach (one-liner):
- Produce a versioned artifact bundle per release that contains all container images, Helm charts, CRD manifests, and optional OS-level packages. Provide a concise index manifest (JSON/YAML) with checksums and install order. Use a small CLI to push bundles to customer airgap registries / object stores and to validate installs.

Non-goals (for this draft):
- Offline OS patching strategy for heterogeneous distributions (defer to customers' patch policies).
- Full automatic image signing integration (we'll support signature verification hooks; signing pipeline TBD).

Bundle composition (recommended layout)
- bundle-v{MAJOR}.{MINOR}.{PATCH}.tar.gz (or .zip for Windows customers)
  - manifest.yaml    # list of images, chart refs, file checksums, install order, semantic version
  - images/          # saved OCI images as tarballs, named by repo_tag and sha256
    - redwood/runtime:v2.3.1@sha256=abc123.tar (note: prefer <name>@sha256 for uniqueness)
  - charts/          # all helm chart packages (.tgz) we deploy (including dependencies)
  - manifests/       # CRDs, static YAMLs we apply before charts
  - scripts/         # install helper scripts for offline nodes (systemctl, kubeadm hints)
  - metadata.json    # small machine-friendly summary (name, version, build_ts, created_by, artifacts_hash)
  - os_packages/     # optional: rpms/debs for helper tools (skopeo, runc, ctr) if customers request

Manifest fields (manifest.yaml):
- release: x.y.z
- created_at: ISO8601
- artifacts_hash: sha256 of entire bundle file
- install_order: [preseed_images, install_registry, apply_manifests, load_images, install_charts, postchecks]
- images: list of {name, tag, digest, filename, checksum, size_bytes}
- charts: list of {chart_name, version, filename, checksum}
- checks: simple commands to run after install (kubectl get pods -n redwood --selector=app=runtime)

Commands and tooling (examples ops will run in airgap environment)
- Mirror images locally (developer machine with internet):
  - skopeo copy docker://ghcr.io/redwood/runtime:v2.3.1 oci:./images/runtime_v2_3_1:latest
  - skopeo sync --src docker --dest-dir ./images --dest oci docker://ghcr.io/redwood/runtime:v2.3.1
- Save OCI tarball for bundle inclusion:
  - ctr-remote image export ./images/runtime_v2_3_1.tar ghcr.io/redwood/runtime:v2.3.1@sha256:...
  - docker save -o images/runtime_v2_3_1.tar ghcr.io/redwood/runtime:v2.3.1:tag
- On customer side (air-gapped host) to preload registry:
  - # run a local registry or put images into customer registry namespace
  - docker load -i runtime_v2_3_1.tar && docker tag ghcr.io/redwood/runtime:v2.3.1 customer.registry.local/redwood/runtime:v2.3.1 && docker push customer.registry.local/redwood/runtime:v2.3.1
  - OR use ctr-remote images import/ctr commands for containerd clusters

Terraform module notes (iface draft)
- Module name: redwood_airgap_bundle
- Purpose: install/upgrade a specific bundle into an air-gapped environment by driving resources the customer will run (e.g. registry bootstrap jobs, object store placements, preseed scripts). The module should not attempt to manage kube-level app objects directly in the customer's cluster; instead it generates validated artifacts and optional bootstrap jobs.

Inputs (proposed):
- bundle_source: string    # local path or s3:// style URL for bundle.tar.gz (string)
- bundle_version: string   # semantic version for logs and gating
- registry_host: string    # customer registry endpoint where images will be pushed
- registry_creds: map (encoded string) # small credential blob (we'll accept base64 to avoid nested objects in final tf plan)
- preseed_mode: string     # [push, provide-script, none] - how module outputs are delivered to customer
- install_namespace: string # default redwood-system
- k8s_context: string      # optional for local integration tests

Outputs (proposed):
- install_script_path: string  # path to generated shell script for ops to run in airgap env
- preseed_report: string      # summary of images/charts preseeded and checksums
- manifest_checksum: string   # sha256 of manifest included in bundle

Implementation notes (tf best practices):
- Keep logic idempotent: module should detect existing image digests in registry and skip push when unchanged.
- Use null_resource / local-exec to call the airgap cli when running from an ops laptop (we'll provide a go binary). Avoid assuming remote exec into customer hosts.
- Provide a dry-run mode that validates bundle contents and produces a report JSON (useful for Security reviews).
- Treat registry_creds as sensitive variable in tf code and document how customers should rotate creds locally.

Upgrade plan (zero-downtime ambition):
1) Publish bundle-vX.Y.Z to release bucket and tag in git (CI produces bundle and manifest.yaml with checksums).
2) Notify ops + customer contact with package index and preflight checklist (shared link or signed manifest).
3) For minor/patch upgrades: prefer in-place chart upgrades with image preseed + rolling restart. For major schema changes, provide a migration job in manifests/migrations/
4) Preseed images into customer registry (push only digests needed for new version; do not remove older digests).
5) Run staging smoke tests (kubectl rollout status, health probes, sample request/response).
6) Canary upgrade path: add a canary helm-release (N=1 replica) with new image, run traffic validation, then promote.
7) Fallback: provide a rollback bundle with explicit deprecation notes; ensure old images remain in registry for at least 30 days.

Validation and acceptance tests (what CI must produce with each bundle)
- manifest.yaml checksum matches artifacts_hash on bundle
- All image tarballs load successfully into a containerd instance in CI smoke runner
- Helm charts lint and render templates with placeholders replaced by values.yaml (render-only check)
- Minimal e2e: start runtime with minimal config and run a short sample request (local cluster)

Security considerations
- Prefer digests over tags in manifest to avoid mutable tags in airgap installs.
- Offer an optional signatures.json (cosign signatures) per-bundle; validation implemented as an install-time hook that can be disabled by enterprise customers.
- Document the trust model clearly (who signs, where signing keys are stored). For customers with HSMs/KMS, provide a pattern for signing the manifest after we ship, so they own final artefact trust anchor.

Storage and bandwidth sizing (rules of thumb)
- Estimate: our runtime + charts + deps ~ 6-12GB per minor release. If supporting multiple versions retained in registry, advise customers to provision 3x expected bundle size for storage to allow temporary caches and GC leeway.
- For extremely constrained environments, provide a delta-bundle mode that includes only image diffs (TBD).

Operational checklist (pre-ship and post-ship)
Pre-ship (Release engineer):
- [ ] run bundle builder pipeline and verify manifest checksums
- [ ] run CI smoke-runner with image load test
- [ ] attach cosign signatures (optional; mark in manifest whether signed)
- [ ] create release note and customer email with install_script and preseed manifest
Post-ship (Customer ops):
- [ ] verify artifacts_hash and manifest signatures (if present)
- [ ] run preseed step (push images into registry) or use provided script
- [ ] apply manifests in order (CRDs -> manifests -> charts)
- [ ] run smoke tests and report results back to Redwood (via support ticket)

Open questions / TODOs (short):
- Decide on canonical artifact storage format: single tar.gz vs directory of files in S3. Single tar.gz is simpler for handoffs but harder to partial-update.
- Delta bundles: how much engineering to support binary diffs (rsync-friendly) vs always full bundles?
- Signature model: integrate cosign vs custom signing pipeline; decide where keys live for enterprise customers.
- Terraform module credentials handling: recommend customers create short-lived tokens for pre-seed operations; provide documented rotation steps.

Risks and mitigations
- Risk: customer registry policies (harbor, artifactory) may reject certain image manifests. Mitigation: create small compatibility test matrix; add a shim that rewrites manifests when safe.
- Risk: mismatched containerd vs docker save formats. Mitigation: include both docker-save and oci-export variants in bundle when practical; document supported tools.

Notes to self (work items):
- Build a minimal golang CLI (airgapctl) to: validate bundle, push images to registry, generate install script, run local dry-run.
- Prototype TF module using local-exec that calls airgapctl; do not over-automate cluster modifications.
- Add example values.yaml for offline installs with environment-specific overrides.

References & links:
- GitHub PR for bundle builder: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/482
- Jira: INFRA-723 for airgap pipeline epic
- Confluence draft: CONFLUENCE-4567 (airgap requirements)

Quick checklist for next sync with Security/RE: share this draft and ask:
- Are cosign signatures acceptable as primary integrity proof?
- Minimum retention policy for old images in customer registries (30/90 days?)
- Support matrix for registries customer-side: docker-registry, harbor, artifactory, ECR-on-prem

End of draft.

(Inline notes: keep this file intentionally conversational — we'll extract a cleaned playbook for the docs site once we finalize the TF interface and the airgapctl prototype.)
